title: This Solid Is 99.8% Air and Caught Dust From a Comet

scenes.text: This solid is ninety-nine point eight percent air.
It's called aerogel, and it's the world's lightest solid.
It's about a thousand times less dense than glass.
NASA flew it to a comet to catch dust moving up to six times faster than a rifle bullet.
The grains buried themselves inside it, leaving tracks up to two hundred times their own length.
A solid that's almost nothing, and it caught pieces of a comet.

description:
This solid is 99.8 percent air.
NASA's Stardust mission used aerogel to catch comet dust moving up to six times faster than a rifle bullet.
What would you build with a solid this light?
first_comment: Bonus: NASA says aerogel gives 39 times more insulation than the best fiberglass. Would you wear a jacket made of it?
